newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian oil firms put petrol prices on hold.
newsitem.headline: Italian oil firms put petrol prices on hold.

text.p: Italian oil firms on Wednesday published a list of petrol pump prices which they promised to hold unchanged for the next eight days.
The oil industry body, Unione Petrolifera, agreed to the price freeze after member companies came under heavy fire from the government for hiking pump tariffs in response to recent dollar gains.
The prices between the distibutors varied between 1,930-1,935 lire per litre of leaded petrol and 1,840-1,845 lire for a litre of unleaded petrol.

A number of companies, including Agip Petroli, a unit of state controlled energy giant Eni, have decided not to introduce a five lire per litre increase announced on Tuesday and have stuck to their original tariffs.
The government, worried that rising petrol prices could ignite inflation, said on Tuesday Italian pump tariffs were "without parallel" in the European Union.
Oil firms have lifted prices in response to dollar strength, with the U.S. currency rising by more than 20 percent against the lira since the start of the year.
Oil is priced in dollars. Unione Petrolifera has said its members have so far have passed on only part of the added costs to their customers.
